title: Natty or not (.com): Eric Bugenhagen
summary: NH goes through a nattyornot.com article claiming Eric Bugenhagen uses steroids, attacking its poor bodyfat estimates, FFMI logic, misleading comparisons to Serge Nubret and Arnold, the treatment of his BFR-pumped 20-inch arms, and its confusion of the Bulgarian method with 'Bulgarian light'. His main target is the 'natural limit' pessimists, whom he sees as just as harmful as fake natties. He argues natural progress continues with rising tonnage, naturals peak around 35-40, and being small is no excuse for a natural.

claims.claim: He won't make 'natty or not' videos about individuals; most such videos come from bitter people who don't look like they lift, though they help newcomers learn what's naturally possible.
Pessimists who say a good physique is impossible naturally hurt new lifters as much as fake natties; it's a loser's mindset.
He believes Eric Bugenhagen is natural, having followed him a long time and seen no signs otherwise.
Estimating bodyfat as '12-15%' is far too wide a range: losing 3% bodyfat while keeping muscle can take a natural years.
Bugenhagen (about 6'1-6'2, 235-240 lbs) is likely 15%+ bodyfat, a healthy level at which naturals look soft without a pump and like marble with one.
FFMI means little: it's too influenced by height and bodyfat error. He was above 25 when overweight and dropped below after losing weight, and PED users can be under 25.
You can't predict someone's shredded weight by subtracting fat: a cut can strip muscle and fat distribution changes.
10% bodyfat is reachable for a natural while staying fairly big if done slowly; cutting fast would make him melt away.
Comparing a natural at 15% with Serge Nubret, who was about 8% and enhanced, is invalid; PEDs changed the game.
Naturals should follow their own rules and carry more bodyfat: it doesn't look bad, keeps them healthy and keeps them big. Getting contest-ripped means sacrificing a lot of mass.
He has a six-pack at 16-17% bodyfat; well-muscled naturals distort how bodyfat looks because muscle bulges through fat.
Bugenhagen competed in powerlifting and has done more orthodox deadlifts and squats than almost anyone on YouTube; odd lifts were a phase he did for fun.
He refuses to fight another man's battle; he made the video to defend natural potential from both PED users and pessimists.
Odd lifts and partials may not be the best muscle builders, but they aren't useless.
Bugenhagen's 20-inch arms came from a BFR (kaatsu) mega-pump that traps blood in the muscle, not a real cold measurement; maybe 18-19 inches cold.
He measures his own muscles cold, without a pump, because his pumped and unpumped sizes differ a lot.
Three years into lifting after puberty his arms were about 13 inches; now they're 18. Size is added around the whole arm, so the 'look at the gap in the tape' argument is meaningless.
You can have abs at 20% bodyfat and fairly defined abs at 15%.
Many 18-year-olds on PEDs reach 20-inch arms; it's ordinary enhanced but a holy grail for naturals. Today's pros have 24-inch arms at sub-10% bodyfat.
You can't predict PED response: some react badly, some barely respond, and full results need staying on for a long time.
Arnold's arm claims are unverifiable since he exaggerated to build his legend; on stage he was sub-10% bodyfat, and 5% bodyfat changes how you look completely.
Joint size only gives a baseline, not a limit: he has very thin wrists and knees but 18-inch arms and 20-inch thighs at 16-17% bodyfat.
He respects natural bodybuilders who compete but will never strip down to a 'skinny skeleton' for stage, because it's pointless when 15% looks good.
Natty pessimists judge naturals by standards set by PED users and have forgotten what natural means.
Subcutaneous fat and water around the muscle make it look bigger, which is good for naturals.
As bodyfat crashes, natural testosterone production crashes and muscle can't be kept, so naturals must be patient and stay in a healthy range.
He considers Mike O'Hearn a known fake natty whose claims shouldn't be used as a natural benchmark; a natural beside a PED user looks very different.
YouTube lifters often peak at 20-25 and then decline because of PEDs, while true naturals peak around 35-40, after accumulating huge tonnage.
Of identical twins, the one training 15 years will be bigger than the one training 5, having accumulated more tonnage.
Somatotypes and a predetermined physiology don't exist as limits; he went from skinny to big.
No study shows a muscle stops growing after a set tonnage; increasing weight, volume and intensity intelligently year after year keeps growing the muscle.
The body is predisposed to store fat rather than build muscle, because fat is an energy reserve and muscle is costly in calories and oxygen, but training and nutrition can overcome this.
When progress slows, quitters separate from winners; naturals spend two hours a day on minimal gains that add up, because they love it.
Hard work doesn't guarantee winning, but it always improves results; working without being smart is just slower and riskier.

The Bulgarian method (Abadjiev) meant multiple daily sessions maxing several lifts, 6-8 hours a day, needing PEDs; the 'Wisconsin/Bulgarian light' approach of maxing once in 45 minutes is low-volume, high-intensity and completely different.
Believing tonnage could double from 30 to 60 million lbs over five years with zero muscle gain is illogical.
He expects to be told both that he's at his natural limit and, when he looks impressive, that he's on PEDs.
Occasional high-intensity work can push progression and help you tolerate more volume, raising tonnage.

'I train hard' is a valid natty argument because fake natties usually don't: leg extensions and grunting aren't hard training. Hard training means volume and intensity on compounds, with supersets, adding up to high tonnage.
In about 10 years of commercial gyms he has never seen anyone outwork him, proof that most people don't train hard; 5x5 heavy deadlifts isn't hard training because tonnage is low.
A natural should aim to be so big, ripped and freaky that people think he's on PEDs.
About 95% of Bugenhagen's training is rigid orthodox lifting.
He doesn't think his own genetics are great, so viewers can reach his physique or beyond; it isn't complicated, just hard and slow.
People call others fake natty to excuse their own laziness; using 'I'm natural' to justify being small after years of training is nearly as bad as being a fake natty.

exercises.name: BFR / kaatsu arm training
exercises.why: traps blood and inflates arm measurements; not a true size measure
